acceptance_signals: The seven newly included test modules no longer require README to duplicate Harness protocol facts, human-pilot details, interview evidence, exhaustive internal file navigation, portfolio evidence, product-site detail, or social-preview ownership that belongs elsewhere.

README retains links or visual references that are genuinely part of the concise product entry, including the product homepage, evidence portfolio, reviewer guide, unbriefed human adoption pilot, and the existing social preview asset without adding more than the three primary first-screen routes.
Exact Harness, pilot, interview, portfolio, site, and social asset claims remain tested at their existing owning documents or assets; no failing test is deleted, skipped, or reduced to a tautology.
The cumulative README refactor remains within the previously admitted product, reference, architecture, and evidence responsibility model and creates no catch-all navigation surface.
Focused documentation tests and the supported full Python 3.11 suite pass, followed by governance, cumulative scope, link, privacy, and diff validation.
STATUS and the dated log record the initial full-suite ownership failures, the admitted corrective scope, final results, pending human comprehension evidence, and no Git or publication authority.

decision.rationale: The accountable human reviewed structured proposal prp-e99afc2fc27a4bd8934fec53ca806022 and admitted that exact task through an explicit admission control.

requirement.summary: Complete the admitted README product-entry refactor by updating the seven additional documentation-oriented test modules discovered by the full suite so they protect the concise product entry, required product and visual routes, and exact protocol or evidence facts at their existing owning surfaces instead of requiring README to remain a catch-all navigation and evidence archive.

items: Updating seven more tests could weaken coverage if assertions are removed without binding the same fact to an owning document or asset.
Restoring every former README link would recreate the navigation monolith and defeat the admitted product-entry outcome.
A social preview or product-site link placed in the first-screen route group could violate the exact three-primary-route acceptance signal.
The cumulative scope must include both admitted task records and all previously modified product-entry files so scope reconciliation remains honest.
User-owned .codex content, public HTML, assets, source code, schemas, release files, and external consumer repositories remain excluded.
Reviewed assumption: The filtered full-suite output correctly localizes all 47 remaining failures to seven additional test modules.
Reviewed assumption: Existing Harness, pilot, interview, portfolio, product-site, and social asset owners still contain the exact facts their tests should protect.
Reviewed assumption: A non-primary social preview image and compact secondary documentation links can remain in README without adding primary first-screen routes.
Reviewed assumption: No product or runtime behavior change is required to correct these responsibility assertions.
Reviewed unknown: Additional stale README-copy assertions may appear only after these seven modules are corrected and the full suite is rerun.
Reviewed unknown: Unbriefed-reader comprehension remains a later human validation outcome and is not established by this test migration.
